definitions.explanation: The cooking process of removing bitter, astringent, or harsh components from vegetables and other ingredients to improve their taste.

examples.japanese: ほうれん{草|そう}は{灰汁|あく}{抜|ぬ}きをしてから{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Remove the bitterness from spinach before using it.

examples.japanese: たけのこの{灰汁|あく}{抜|ぬ}きには{米|こめ}ぬかを{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Use rice bran to remove the harshness from bamboo shoots.

examples.japanese: {灰汁|あく}{抜|ぬ}きを{怠|おこた}ると{苦味|にがみ}が{残|のこ}る。
examples.english: If you skip removing the bitterness, the bitter taste will remain.

notes:
FORMATION: {灰汁|あく} (lye; harsh/bitter components) + {抜|ぬ}き (removing).

COOKING TECHNIQUE: Essential preparation step in Japanese cuisine for many vegetables.

COMMON METHODS:
・{茹|ゆ}でて{灰汁|あく}を{取|と}る (boil and skim off scum)
・{水|みず}に{晒|さら}す (soak in water)
・{塩水|しおみず}に{漬|つ}ける (soak in salt water)
・{米|こめ}ぬかと{茹|ゆ}でる (boil with rice bran)

COMMON INGREDIENTS REQUIRING {灰汁|あく}{抜|ぬ}き:
・ほうれん{草|そう} (spinach)
・たけのこ (bamboo shoots)
・{蕨|わらび} (bracken fern)
・ごぼう (burdock root)
・なす (eggplant)

RELATED: {灰汁|あく}を{取|と}る (skim off scum from simmering food)
